Ciao Lucia Takes Its Signature Sun-Soaked Wardrobe Into Fall

September 7, 2026 | Written by Andrea Spanik
Share This:

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:44
Instaread

The Vibe :

⊹ Ciao Lucia shifts its vacation-minded wardrobe toward cooler weather without dropping the dresses.

⊹ Silk, cotton voile, wool knits, corduroy, and poplin all appear in the current arrivals.

⊹ Striped separates sit beside black dresses, chamomile tones, and denim-colored wool.

⊹ Dresses remain prominent, but knits and pants give the lineup a more transitional wardrobe.

Ciao Lucia is heading into fall without suddenly pretending vacation season never happened. The Los Angeles label’s current arrivals keep dresses firmly in rotation, but silk and cotton voile now share space with wool knits, corduroy, chino, and heavier striped pieces. The Beverly Black Georgette Silk Dress and Jonita Chamomile Cotton Voile Dress keep one foot in the brand’s warm-weather world, while the Rianne Canard Wool Blend Pullover signals that the wardrobe is officially changing seasons.

Stripes do some of the connecting work. The Delan Stripe Cotton Poplin Top pairs naturally with the Kaila Stripe Cotton Poplin Pant, while the Lorene Venice Stripe Knit Cardigan takes the pattern into knitwear. The Yuli Venice Stripe Corduroy Pant pushes things further into fall, giving Ciao Lucia’s normally breezy styling a little more weight. Dresses still dominate the wider Ciao Lucia dress edit, but this drop makes a strong argument for keeping pants and sweaters nearby.

The material mix gets broader from there. The Tilda Denim Wool Blend Dress introduces a denim-colored wool option, the Mariko Khaki Chino Short keeps tailoring in the picture, and the Mirey Black Dupioni Dress adds another evening-facing fabric to the assortment. It all sits comfortably inside the wider Ciao Lucia lineup: still sun-minded, just ready for a jacket once dinner runs late.

Brand DNA

Founded in Sydney in 2001, Shona Joy channels Australian glamour through fluid dresses, polished tailoring, satin, lace, and hand-painted prints. Feminine silhouettes and a subtle ’70s mood give the label its refined approach to occasion dressing.

About The Author

  • Andrea Spanik

    From fashion and beauty to health and wellness, she enjoys sharing and connecting on the topics that help to make our everyday lives just a bit brighter. If you don't find her behind her laptop writing her latest article, you'll also find her walking her dog, whipping up a new recipe, or scouring the mall for the latest trends. Andrea's experience in fashion began after graduating from the Fashion Marketing and Merchandising program from the Academy of Design in Toronto, ON. She broke out into the competitive world of fashion by launching her own online boutique, selling women's clothing and accessories. From there, very quickly, she discovered online selling was not for her. She now prefers to stay behind the computer, chatting about fashion in a written format that still allows her to connect with fellow style enthusiasts. And, since then, she has never looked back, writing for independent magazines, small businesses, and everything in between. Andrea now also occasionally writes for companies and brands outside the fashion and beauty industry, but at the end of the day, her heart remains loyal to what she knows best—great fashion.
